key: And though man be risen up to pursue thee, and to seek thy soul, yet the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life with the LORD thy God; and the souls of thine enemies, them shall he sling out, as from the hollow of a sling.
s: Pleading with David not to avenge Nabal’s insult by bloodshed, Abigail foretells his kingdom; Radak, on 25:29, reads ‘bundle of life’ as David kept alive against his pursuers, walking in God’s ways all his days, and Metzudat David, on 25:29, as the soul’s eternal, spiritual life once it parts from the body.

reason: verse.js ok, ref 1 Samuel 25:29 and at [256,29] match. Plain sense faithful: Abigail pleads with David (25:24 to 31) to keep from bloodguilt over Nabal, and foretells a sure house (25:28) and his appointment as prince over Israel (25:30); no four-word run from the key. Read every packet source on 25:29 and Radak, Rashi and Metzudat David across 25:21 to 34. Radak’s own explanation is this-worldly: his pursuers cannot kill him and he will be in life with God, walking in His ways all his days (he then reports Targum Jonathan and the Sages taking it of the world to come, without adopting it as his own). Metzudat David takes it of the eternal, spiritual life after the soul parts from the body. The two genuinely differ and the sentence names both without resolving. Rashi glosses only the sling.
